subject: SLA, on-call routing & credit structure for premium support
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@datawave.ai>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 14:02:00 +0000
Subject: Premium support — uptime tiers, response SLAs, and pricing question

Hi Naomi,

Thanks for the demo last week. The team is evaluating Redwood for inference serving and we need clarity on your premium support packaging. Two things are top of mind for execs and procurement:

- Uptime guarantees by region (we run critical workloads in eu-west-1 and eu-central-1).
- Response time ladders (P1/P2/P3) and who is on-call during regional incidents / escalation handoffs.

Can you send a short proposal that maps: uptime tier -> response SLA -> what escalation coverage looks like (hours, phone/SMS, named escalations), and the pricing for each band? We have a rough budget for FY27 and are also asking about discounts for a 12‑month committed spend (~$600k).

If possible, include sample credits/penalties and a suggested contract clause for fallback model variants (we need a way to degrade gracefully if primary capacity is exhausted).

Appreciate a one-page view and an estimate so procurement can model it.

Elena

--
Elena Rossi
Head of Cloud Ops, DataWave
elena.rossi@datawave.ai
+44 20 7946 0xxx
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@datawave.ai>
Cc: procurement@datawave.ai
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 17:18:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Premium support — uptime tiers, response SLAs, and pricing question

Hi Elena — thanks for the clear ask and for the time last week.

Attached is a concise proposal (SLA_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf) that maps three availability bands we offer and the corresponding response / escalation coverage. Highlights:

- Bronze (99.5% monthly): standard support, ticket route, 8x5 email/Ticket response (P1: 4h initial, P2: 8h, P3: 48h).
- Silver (99.9% monthly): accelerated routing, 24x7 triage for P1 via phone/SMS, named escalation to L2 oncall within 60m, P2 initial 4h.
- Gold (99.99% monthly): dedicated reserved capacity option, 24x7 phone + immediate pager for P1, named oncall escalation matrix with direct SL escalation to NOC lead within 15m, plus automatic capacity burst fallback to compatible model variants.

Pricing: we price support as a % uplift on committed inference spend (examples in the sheet) — typical uplift ranges are 6% (Bronze), 12% (Silver), 22% (Gold) on committed monthly runrate. For 12‑month commits we can consider tiered discounts: 5% off Silver at $600k annual, up to 10% off Gold if you commit $1.2M+.

Credits: our standard credit matrix is in the doc (scaled by duration and % below target). We can add a contractual fallback clause for model variant degradation — suggested wording included in the redlines doc.

Quick Q: to tailor the pricing precisely — can you confirm your expected average RPS and typical token/session lengths for the high‑priority workloads? Also, do you plan for multi‑region active-active or active-passive?

If procurement wants, I can set up a 30‑minute call Friday to walk through the sheet.

Best,
Naomi
Naomi Feldman
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: SLA_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 10:07:00 -08:00
Subject: Fwd: Premium support — pricing request (DataWave)

Ben / Marcus — forwarding DataWave's request and my draft offer. Key asks: 12‑month commit ~$600k target, eu footprint, want clarity on named escalation and fallback to lower‑quality model variants.

My proposed public-facing offer (from the sheet): Silver w/ 5% commit discount at $600k. They asked if we can do a one‑time onboarding credit and a 30% discount on on‑call hours for first 3 months. Margin-wise, what flexibility do we have on Gold at that commit size?

Also: they specifically want the fallback model variant clause copied into the MSA; I attached Draft_MSA_redlines.docx with suggested language.

Would appreciate your suggestions on concessions (onboarding credit amount, transient on‑call discount, and whether to cap credits).

—Naomi
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>
To: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 13:42:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Premium support — pricing request (DataWave)

Thanks for the context. My quick take:

- Approve Silver + 5% commit discount at $600k — healthy and keeps room for expansion.
- For Gold, margin is thin at $1.2M with a 10% cut; I would only authorize deeper discount if they commit to reserved capacity (we should make burst credits conditional on paid reserved nodes).
- Onboarding credit: approve a one‑time $25k implementation credit (applied to first invoice).
- On‑call hours discount: we shouldn't discount time-based oncall beyond 15% — instead offer 50% off first month for oncall OT as a short-term concession.
- Credits cap: yes, cap SLA credits at 6 months of support uplift to limit downside exposure.

Also confirm that the fallback model clause limits functional degradation (we should require a minimum perplexity/response correctness SLA tied to a test prompt set). Ask legal to mark that in the MSA redlines.

If DataWave pushes hard, we can trade a 1% extra discount for a 24‑month commit.

Ben
Senior Director, Commercial Strategy
From: Naomi Feldman <naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@datawave.ai>, procurement@datawave.ai
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Premium support — uptime tiers, response SLAs, and pricing question

Elena — thanks for the quick responses on the call this morning. Per our discussion, here's the concise counteroffer and next steps:

Counteroffer summary (attached SLA_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf and Draft_MSA_redlines.docx):
- Offer: Silver band (99.9%) with named escalation matrix and 24x7 P1 triage, priced at 12% uplift on committed spend.
- Commit: $600k annual committed spend (12 months).
- Discount: 5% off the Silver uplift for the commit.
- One‑time onboarding credit: $25,000 applied to the first invoice.
- On‑call OT concession: 50% discounted oncall overtime for month 1 only.
- SLA credits: standard credit matrix applies, capped at 6 months of support uplift.
- Fallback: included clause permitting temporary routing to compatible, lower‑latency model variants; must pass DataWave's PROMPT_SET_v1 acceptance tests (we included suggested test and acceptance criteria in redlines).

Next steps:
1) If this works, procurement: please confirm acceptance of the financials and we will route the Draft_MSA_redlines to Legal for a quick review.
2) Naomi will schedule a 30‑minute implementation scoping call next Tue to gather RPS and token/session distributions (we need that to size reserved capacity if they decide).
3) If DataWave prefers a 24‑month commit in lieu of the onboarding credit, we can consider an additional 1% discount on the uplift.

Happy to jump on a call if you want to walk the sheet live.

Best regards,
Naomi
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
naomi.feldman@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0134

Attachments: SLA_pricing_sheet_v2.pdf, Draft_MSA_redlines.docx
